newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks likely to rise after Dow rebound.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks likely to rise after Dow rebound.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to rise in Tuesday's session following a rebound on Wall Street and gains posted by Nikkei futures in Chicago overnight, brokers said. However, they added that the rise was likely to be limited as there are few factors to prompt buying.
On Monday, the 225-share Nikkei average shed 154.51 points or 0.87 percent to close at 17,692.47. Its June futures ended 190 points lower at 17,640.
"The indices will probably start out in positive range as futures try to catch up with the Chicago close," a market analyst at a foreign brokerage said.
Overnight in New York, the Dow industrials rose about 60 points after falling nearly 150 on Friday. Nikkei 225 futures added 50 points to close at 17,740 in Chicago.
Brokers hoped that the rebound in U.S. stocks would revive the blue-chip rally, which has been showing signs of fizzing out in recent sessions.

"Apart from blue chips there is nothing else worth buying," Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager said. "Once profit-taking brings the share prices down to a moderate level, bargain hunters will appear to push it back up again."

Brokers said that apart from the buy backs of banks and real estate issues and purchases of blue chips on the back of strength on Wall Street, a "Big Four" brokerage celebrating its business centennial was actively placing orders for a wide range of shares and supporting the market.
"A bunch of issues, including Fujitsu Ltd, Nippon Steel Corp and NKK Corp, rallied due to buy orders from the brokerage, surprising the market," a trader at a "Big Four" brokerage said.
Fujitsu rose 10 yen to 1,290, and Nippon Steel added one yen to 360.
NKK was down two yen at 258 by midday.
Market sources said that investors were likely to continue pursuing issues backed by solid earnings, after the bank buy-back phase wanes and indices start to dip.

"Apart from blue chips which are symbolised by Sony Corp, there is nothing else worth buying at the moment," Yasuo Ueki, Nikko Securities general manager said. "Once profit-taking brings the share prices down to a moderate level, bargain hunters will appear to push it back up again."
Sony was flat at 8,950 after rising as high as 9,010 early in the session.
Banks, fisheries, sea transport, credit/lease and real estate were at the top of the list of advancing sectors. There were no sectors posting major losses.
